content.thinking:
I'm planning the realistic proportions for the monster truck—roughly 3.5m tall with 1.7m tires, 3.6m wide, 5.5m long—and thinking through how to build it with simple box and cylinder geometry in a pixel-art style, keeping the implementation robust and low-risk.

I'm working out the joint hierarchy: a root chassis node with hinge joints for steering and wheel spin, figuring out axle positions, track width, and wheelbase so the wheels sit correctly relative to the body and chassis rails.

For the wheel geometry, I'm orienting the cylinders along the X axis for the axle, then placing tread lugs around each wheel's circumference using X-axis rotation to position boxes radially. I'm considering whether to merge all lugs per wheel into a single geometry to keep the part count manageable instead of instancing each one separately.

For the tyre sidewall, I'm designing a small pixel texture with concentric rings representing the rubber, stripes, rim, and lug nuts, mapped onto a circle geometry placed facing outward on each wheel's outer face.

Since texture orientation doesn't matter much given symmetric bolt patterns, I'm focusing on the tire paint approach: a rubber color ramp with dithered noise applied via a cell-paint function, with the cylinder geometry receiving this texture directly as it's generated.

For the body, I'm designing a pixel-art monster truck with flame livery—a pickup-style silhouette with hood, cab, and lifted bed, using a red-orange body color against yellow-orange flame accents and steel/chrome trim. I'm planning to construct the flames by painting continuous patterns across the body's box geometry using a position-based cell paint function rather than separate textured panels.

Still tuning flame geometry...

I'll add a white racing stripe on top using the local x-coordinate, and since flames mirror symmetrically I don't need to worry about sign there. Now I'm laying out the body geometry—starting with the lower tub as a long box spanning the chassis length with specific width and height bounds, keeping wheel clearance in mind.

Checking wheel positions against the body, the wheels sit outboard of the body's x-range so they won't intersect even though they overlap vertically. I'm raising the body slightly to sit above the wheel tops, then considering whether to add fender flare boxes over the wheels, but deciding simpler shapes may suffice for now.

The caps overlap the body nicely, so I'll extend them to connect fully, maybe adding a front and rear lip box too. Now I'm laying out the main cab and hood structure, defining the lower tub dimensions and hood front position for the pickup body.

Still working out dimensions...

I'm sizing the cab height so the roof sits around 3.05m, keeping proportions sensible against the wheel diameter. For the windows, I'm planning dark interior boxes for depth plus separate glass panes on the sides with a pixel-art diagonal glint pattern to fake reflections without actual transparency.

Now I'm figuring out the doors: hinge joints on each side with a door panel, window pane, and handle attached, sized to sit slightly proud of the cab's lower body so they read as distinct parts. I'm also working out how the flame paint job wraps onto the door panels and making sure the cab lower box doesn't visually clash with the door thickness, then moving to the rear bed with floor and side wall boxes.

I'm adding the tailgate, front bed wall, a tubular roll cage with an integrated light bar glowing yellow on the roof, plus glow effects for headlights, taillights, and flame exhaust details. For the exhaust I'm placing two chrome pipe rods angled behind the cab with small glowing flame tips at the top.

Now I'm building out the front end: a heavy black bumper with grille texture, glowing headlight squares, a winch, skid plate, and a supercharger blower scoop on the hood for that classic monster truck look, before starting the ladder frame chassis rails.

I'm working out the suspension system now -- cylindrical front and rear axles with spherical differential housings, mounted statically to the chassis, feeding into steering knuckles at each wheel. For the shocks I'm planning paired coilover rods per side per axle, angled from axle to frame, with a striped cylinder look to simulate the coil spring pattern.

I also need to be careful with bone assignment for the shock rod sweeps -- since bones default to the nearest joint to the start point, shocks placed near the axle could accidentally snap to the wrong joint (like the wheel joint instead of the chassis), so I'll need to check the actual joint coordinates to avoid that misassignment.

Rather than rely on auto-detection, I'll explicitly pass a bone argument whenever creating a part. I'll write wrapper functions that always specify the bone (chassis, wheel joint, etc.) so parts like hubs and steering joints attach correctly, and think through how hinge orientation and roll should be set for the wheel's spin axis.

Now I'm sketching out joint naming: chassis as root, wheelFL/FR/RL/RR as hinge joints, with steerFL/steerFR parenting the front wheels, mirroring left/right across +X, and assigning hinge roles to wheels, doors, and the tailgate.

I'm also planning the interior details — seats, dashboard, a steering wheel made from a torus, and a tiny pixel driver wearing a bright helmet visible through the windshield, plus exterior touches like mud flaps, tow hooks, and door decals.

For the decal, I'm sketching out a pixel-font number plate ("07" on a white plate with black digits) to place on each door, working out how the plane orientation should face outward so the text reads correctly from outside rather than mirrored.

I'm also planning a few more texture details: a checker-flag pattern on the tailgate, vertical bars for the grille, and a darker mud-streak treatment near the bottom of the body to add grime.

Adding mud and tire details...

That tangential offset gives a slightly lower corner, but the sink allowance of 0.064 covers it fine, and the tilt doesn't push it further down. For the tyre, I'm going with a 16-segment faceted cylinder at radius 0.78, checking how the facet distance compares to the true radius.

Now I'm designing the tyre's sidewall texture: a circular overlay mapped onto the cylinder cap, where pixel distance from center determines whether it's rubber with lettering dashes, a thin stripe, a chrome rim with lug bolts, or the center cap.

Finishing the hub center with a darker chrome tone, and confirming the same texture works for both wheel faces without needing separate rotation logic. I'll skip a separate 3D hub boss geometry since the texture detail already conveys the lug nuts and cap convincingly enough.

Setting up imports for the build file, pulling in geometry merging utilities and pixel/paint helper functions, while being careful to avoid unused imports since those throw errors. I'm defining a snapColor helper to quantize colors to a limited palette, keeping the overall color count low since paints don't count against the budget.

Writing color ramps...

Still writing mud splash logic...

Now I'm adding a navy-edged white stripe decal on the top-facing panels like the hood, roof, and bed floor, keeping it off the fender caps. For the side faces I'm computing a flame pattern using a sawtooth wave scaled by height and depth to create a jagged flickering edge along the body.

Tuning the flame geometry so the tongues lean backward as they rise, with amplitude scaling by z-position so the flames are tallest on the hood and tub but still lick up slightly onto the doors without overshooting, then layering an orange base flame with a smaller yellow flame inside using a hot color ramp.

For the base paint, I'm defining a default red shading that lightens on top faces, darkens on sides, and adds subtle speckle noise, with dithering enabled for smoother gradients, plus a thin dark red-brown outline along the flame edges. For texture density I'm checking that the shared paint atlas (bumping to 2048, effectively 4096) gives enough texels per cell across the painted body and tire areas so detail doesn't look blurry, while watching for wasted space on tiny box faces.

Setting up the body-building functions now.

Still writing box helper...

Positioning the wheel hubs with portal gear boxes where the axle meets the wheel, then wiring up the suspension geometry: four-link bars connecting axle to frame on each side, plus shock absorbers running from the axle up to the body underside.

I realize the shocks can poke outside the tub through the gap between the tub edge and wheel, around x≈1.05, giving a classic exposed-monster-truck-shock look. I'm defining each shock as a layered rod: a thicker striped spring section near the bottom transitioning to a thinner chrome shaft near the top, with mounting brackets at both ends and positioned at slight z-offsets per wheel.

For the fenders, I'm sketching painted caps above each wheel arch, sized roughly 1.1 wide and stretching from the body gap outward, sitting just under the hood height so they read as classic flared fenders, and checking that tire extents don't overrun the tub's front edge too much.

Now I'm placing the front grille panel as a thin box between the hood and bumper, sizing it around 1.5 wide and 0.7 tall with a slight thickness, and figuring out how to texture it so the grille pattern reads correctly given the aspect ratio.

I'm designing the grille texture with a chrome frame, dark bar slats, and a small diamond-shaped badge in the center, then positioning the headlight boxes with chrome bezels on either side within the grille's x bounds, giving them a warm glow color. Next I'm sketching out the bumper's top bar as a black steel box positioned beneath the grille.

For the bumper, I'm adding chrome bull bar rods angled from the bumper up toward the grille with a connecting crossbar, plus a small winch box and fairlead up front and red tow hook rods. I'm refining the main bumper shape into a dark steel plate with a dithered scratched-metal texture and bolt studs, and considering layering a yellow-and-black diagonal hazard stripe pattern on its front face.

Then I'm moving to hood details -- building the blower box, an intake scoop with a black box and chrome rim frame, chrome stack cylinders along the blower top, thin hinge-line boxes along the hood sides, and rows of small dark louvre boxes on either side of the hood.

Now I'm laying out the cab: a lower body box sized to stay flush with the tub, a dark interior core box, an upper cab shell, and a roof slab that sits above it, then I'm starting on the A-pillars at the windshield sides.

Adding windshield and pillar geometry...

To actually show the driver and steering wheel, I should make the windshield mostly transparent with just streak highlights and edge glints via alpha cutout, rather than a solid opaque texture. That way the cab interior—seats, floor, back wall—remains visible through the glass.

I'm designing a dithered glass texture: using a bayer pattern so about a quarter of pixels get a dark blue tint, creating a screen-door transparency effect, with diagonal glint streaks layered in a lighter blue-white for the pixel-art shine.

Now I'm positioning the glass panels: side door windows, rear quarter windows, and door frames with proper hinge joints and body-colored tube rails, keeping paint continuous across door seams so flame patterns don't break. I'm also working out the B-pillar and quarter window placement along the chassis, deciding dimensions for the glass boxes at each z-offset.

Next I'm adding door hardware -- chrome handles, seam lines, side mirrors with stalks, and a door number decal that sits over the flame graphics without clipping through the body panels. Then I'm shifting focus to the roof, designing a light bar with a dark frame and glowing lamp boxes mounted across the front, plus brackets and a sun visor piece.

Now I'm figuring out the roof vent, antenna, and a whip flag -- deciding to approximate the flag as a single thin textured box instead of fighting with double-sided plane geometry, since a box naturally shows the texture on all faces without the mirroring headache.

Then I'm laying out the truck bed: the liner floor, side walls, front wall, and tailgate panel, positioning each relative to the tub's dimensions. I'm planning paint logic so the tailgate gets a distinct checker/hazard stripe treatment instead of the default body color, and sketching the rear roll bar as paired tubular uprights with a top crossbar plus a cluster of round rear lights.

I'm adding chrome exhaust stacks with angled caps and glowing orange flame cones at their tips, tuning their height so the flames sit just above the stack openings. Then I'm placing tail lamps on the tailgate, a rear steel bumper with a hitch ball, and black mud flaps positioned just behind the rear wheels to match the wheel's rearward extent.

Now I'm working out matching mud flaps for the front wheels, positioning them just behind the front wheel's lower rear edge.

Then I'm moving to the interior: the floor and lower cab body hide most of it, so I only need visible seating geometry in the upper window band, placing a seat base and seatback box roughly within that visible range.

Next I'm adding a dashboard box with simple dial decals, a tilted steering wheel torus positioned for a left-side driver, and a driver head box, keeping all these elements within the 2.55–3.0 window zone so nothing clips through the roof.

For the driver's suit I'll go with blue to contrast the red car, maybe yellow helmet, and skip adding a passenger mannequin. I'll consider sticker details like tire sidewall decals and hood numbers, but skip extra sponsor decals on the quarter panel to keep things simple.

For the bed I'm adding chrome-blue nitro tank cylinders with striped caps, positioned symmetrically. For lighting, I'm placing fog lights on the bumper and four warm-white glowing cylinders along the roll bar behind the cab, working out their positions relative to the roof height.

I'm sketching the overall vertical build-up — roll bar, exhaust flames, antenna — landing on roughly 3.65m total height, matching real monster truck proportions around 12 feet. Then I'm shifting to the wheel construction function, defining steer and wheel joints on the chassis with the steer joint parented first and the wheel joint attached to it, followed by the tyre cylinder geometry oriented along the x-axis with painted color and proper bone binding.

Working out lug placement math...

Still writing lug geometry...

Checking lug row offsets fit within the tyre width without overlapping, and now considering how to place the wheel decal circles symmetrically on both sides of the wheel.

Actually that hides the shoulder lugs under the decal, so I should shrink the decal radius to .6 covering just the rim and inner sidewall, leaving the shoulder lugs visible from r .62 to .8. I'm reworking the texture scale (20px = 0.6m, .03 per px) so the rubber ring, white stripe, and rim sit at proportionally realistic radii for a monster truck wheel.

Now I'm laying out the rim zones: beyond r=20 is transparent, r14.2-20 is sidewall rubber with lettering and an edge highlight, r12.2-14.2 is a chrome beadlock ring with 16 silver bolts, r5.5-12.2 is the rim face with five spoke cutouts, and r2.8-5.5 is a yellow-orange accent hub ring to complement the red body.

For the very center I'm adding a chrome hub with a dark nut below r1.2, and deciding the decal doesn't need mirroring. I'm scrapping the separate hub cap cylinder since it would hide decal detail, letting the decal handle that look instead, with the beadlock already covered by the decal layer.

Writing tire paint shader...

Checking cell size against triangle budget, confirming wheels sit at correct world coordinates with no front steering pose needed, and deciding brake discs/calipers are unnecessary since they're hidden under the decal. I'm also noting the various textures needed (grille, gauge, glass, number, flag, wheel) and confirming box-geometry parts with cellPaint coloring work fine, plus hazard lights on the bumper. Tallying up roughly 150-200 parts total with low triangle count before moving on to the hood scoop tilt.

Now I'm considering a bull bar accessory and deciding to skip skull ornaments, and adding a drive shaft rod running from the front differential to the rear axle underneath the tub. I'm also confirming the glow effect works on flat-colored parts, and working out the cone geometry for exhaust flames -- using a 4-sided pyramidal cone for a pixelated look, with an inner yellow flame nested inside a larger outer one, positioned right above the exhaust tip.

I'm now defining the hinge joints: left and right doors mounted on the chassis near the top, a tailgate hinge at the rear, and a hood hinge up front with the hood slab and louvres attached while the blower sticks through from the chassis underneath (just like real monster trucks). I'm also placing a steering wheel joint angled toward the driver, and tallying up the part count -- four main wheels plus two steerable ones, the chassis body, two doors, and the tailgate.

Writing door and window code...

Now I'm working out the roof dimensions and position, then moving to the hood slab size and placement at the front of the cab, figuring out where the tub section connects.

I'm skipping minor details like cowl geometry, air dams, and side steps since monster trucks don't typically have those features, but adding a side cage rail running from front to rear along the tub's exterior for structural framing.

Looking at wheel spacing, I place nerf bar rods with brackets in the gap between the front and rear wheels. For the chassis rails I'll use a plain steel color rather than a patterned paint, keeping things simple since area budget matters. For the shock springs I'm setting up an alternating orange/yellow stripe pattern based on vertical position to simulate coil wraps, then starting to build a pixel-art gauge cluster texture with dark background and circular gauge faces.

Writing pixel texture code...

Adding diagonal glint pattern...

Now I'm setting up the tire sidewall decal, using a Bayer threshold pattern for dashes, then starting the main truck build script with helper functions for boxes and joints, making sure types line up with the Joint import.

Adding cylinder and rod helpers...

Writing body paint function...

Still writing color logic... I'm noticing an issue where the top surfaces of the hood and roof are picking up unintended striping.

Still defining paint zones...

Still writing bumper paint logic...

Defining chrome paint variations and positioning the wheels, then setting up a shock absorber function to handle each axle side.

I'm working through the shock mount geometry so it fits properly against the tub side without clipping, then adding the light bar on the roof with eight lamps and chrome roll bar uprights behind the cockpit.

Still writing roll bar geometry...

Adding exhaust clamps, chrome tips, and small flame cones above the stacks, keeping the roll bar and exhaust heights aligned at 3.3.

Adding more vehicle details...

Adjusting the helmet geometry, then adding a dark visor with a small white glint for highlight, and starting a stripe detail on top.

Now I'm placing the arms and gloves relative to the shoulders and torso, connecting them to hands gripping the steering wheel rim, and double-checking torso and head bounds line up correctly on the seat.

Still working out the steering wheel geometry...

Adding a gauge display plane with a white screen texture, skipping the door panel and hidden engine, then moving to bed items like nitro bottle cylinders.

Adjusting toolbox position and adding a handle rod with tools inside; also planning nerf rails, tow hooks, and a front license plate box reusing the number plate texture on the bumper.

I'm positioning the plate on the bumper front center, avoiding the winch which I'm moving lower, and adding red tow hooks plus small glowing fog light squares on either side, carefully matching the bumper's z-depth so everything sits flush on the front face.

Now I'm laying out the bull bars connecting the bumper top to above the grille, sizing the chrome grille panel to fit between the headlight bezels while standing proud of the hood's front fascia, and placing the engine blower and intake boxes on the hood with a chrome trim rim around the top.

I'm adding slotted hood vents along both sides of the hood bone, double-checking that the blower height clears the hood slab properly, and noting the hood hinge position relative to the cab joint. I'm ready to move into writing out the full color palette and code now.

Writing wheel rim texture...

Writing plate border and mud flap details...

Now I'm working through the axle components—diff pumpkin, cover plate, pinion yoke—and moving on to hub geometry.

Placing hub cylinders on the steer joint for front and chassis for rear, adding a track rod connecting the knuckles across the front axle. Now I'm ready to assemble the full file, using naming conventions like wheelFL for front-left.

I'm working through the tailgate details - a gate panel with chrome handle, glowing tail lights and reverse lights - then moving to the bed walls, calculating box dimensions so the tub exterior and gate align properly with the chassis coordinates.

Now I'm positioning the cab's rear window and pillars, placing a dark glass box with a backing wall behind it, and adding C-pillars at the sides to frame the glass edges correctly.

Moving on to quarter windows and side glass placement, checking x-coordinates to align with doors while keeping the glass transparent so interior isn't occluded. I decide to skip extra details like fender liners and window trims to keep things simple.

Finally I'm double-checking types and imports across the code -- confirming `rotation` and `dir`/`at` parameters match expected vector types, that mesh parts expose the right properties for glow effects, and that texture utilities like bayer and cellPaint are actually used so nothing is left unused.

Writing shock absorber geometry...
